name: SemanticNoChange
applies_after_fresh_preconditions_to: ConfirmCustomerAccountCodeSharedClaim when target already has the exact active claim and reviewed conflict still exists
rule: After command-specific identity/revision/lifecycle/security preconditions pass inside the UnitOfWork, compare the requested accepted authoritative state with the current state using the command's exact stored semantics. If they are identical, insert only the LLD-01 command_receipt with result_type='NO_CHANGE', COMMIT, and return current target identity/revision. Do not increment a revision, close/open a relationship, create/supersede an identifier, append lifecycle evidence, or insert an application audit event.

equality.customer_account_code: same active value_text and match_key already belong to the target Customer; other existing shared claimants do not turn an already-present target claim into a change
equality.contact_name: stored accepted name text and derived match key are identical
equality.contact_channel: same owned active channel identity, stored accepted value_text and match_key are identical
equality.contact_affiliation: requested customer_org_id equals the exact current affiliation target, including null/unbound
equality.customer_or_dispatch_descriptive: all governed requested stored fields and derived keys equal current values
equality.setting: same registered contract name/version and SettingDefinition semantic_equals(current_value, requested_value)=true

non_applicable: Create* commands allocate new identity and therefore are not semantic no-ops
ArchiveReference requires active target; already archived is a lifecycle-precondition failure rather than NO_CHANGE
ReactivateReference requires archived target; already active is a lifecycle-precondition failure rather than NO_CHANGE
ArchiveContactChannel requires active channel; already archived is not NO_CHANGE
ReassignCustomerAccountCode changes ownership while its source claim exists and therefore is not a no-op
retry_safety: The committed NO_CHANGE receipt binds command_id and request_hash. A lost-response retry returns the original NO_CHANGE result even if later unrelated commands change the target, preventing an old retry from becoming a new mutation.
history_rule: No-change operator intent is technical idempotency evidence in command_receipts only; it is not fabricated as domain lifecycle or 'manual change' audit evidence because no authoritative fact changed.
